summary: A data table. Table owns the scroll container and density; rows and cells are composed.
useWhen: showing records with more than one attribute worth comparing across rows

useInstead.when: each item is a self-contained summary rather than a row of fields
it is a layout grid rather than data
useInstead.why: a <table> announces row and column semantics that a layout does not have

composition.note: Table > TableHead/TableBody > TableRow > TableCell, matching how Figma layers Table Row > Table Cell > Cell Text. TableHead and TableBody take no props of their own; they place the rows and give TableCell its head-or-body context.

compact.use: dense operational tables where row count matters more than comfort

relaxed.use: short tables where each row deserves attention

guarantees: the scroll container is keyboard reachable, which overflow alone does not provide (WCAG 2.1.1)
requires: `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` on Table — it names the scroll region, and the container takes no props of its own, so this is the only place the name can live
an accessible name on every row-selection Checkbox — those have no visible label by design
notes: Prefer a visible <caption> referenced by aria-labelledby when the table's name should also be seen.

antiPatterns.why: the scroll region is announced with no name, and a keyboard user reaching it is told nothing about what they have entered
screen readers cannot associate data cells with their column

antiPatterns.dont: wrapping Table in your own overflow container
antiPatterns.why: Table already owns the scroll container and makes it focusable; a second one is unreachable by keyboard
every row announces an unnamed checkbox

missingStates.note: Table has no empty, loading or error state of its own — those are the caller's, and they are the states most often forgotten. Pattern coverage is planned; see docs/agent-readiness-plan.md phase 4a.
